first_impression.reaction: Came in from a Google search for a guest list template. The intro gets straight to it: no sign-up, works in Sheets, and it already has flights, accommodation and visa letters. Half our guests are flying in, so that is exactly the bit every generic template misses. No fairytale language, no pop-up feel. I'd download it and keep skimming.

journey.quote: Ours downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up, opens in Google Sheets as well, and carries the travel columns a destination wedding needs: flights, arrival and departure, accommodation and visa letters.
journey.reaction: Good. No email wall, and it already thinks about international guests. That's us.

journey.quote: Household ID. One code for everyone who shares an invitation, such as H001. It lets the Summary tab count households as well as people, which is the number your stationer needs.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of practical detail I trust. Someone has actually run a list before.

journey.quote: A preference changes a plate; an allergy changes how the kitchen works.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and it reads like someone who has dealt with a venue kitchen.

journey.section: Excel and Google Sheets setup: Dropdowns
journey.quote: The four event columns offer the five reply options.
journey.reaction: Earlier it said each event cell takes Not invited, Invited, Attending or Declined. That's four. Which is it? Small, but I notice this kind of thing and it makes me wonder what else is loose.

journey.quote: Visa letter needed and Visa letter sent. Mark Yes when a guest asks you for a letter for their visa application, then Yes again once you have sent it.
journey.reaction: I hadn't even thought about guests needing invitation letters for visas. Useful, and the line that visa rules belong to each guest is honest.

journey.quote: Transport to venue needed. Yes or No, so you have the number of people who will need a way to reach the venue once you start planning that part of the weekend.
journey.reaction: This is the grandparents-from-the-airport problem. A column tells me how many, but I still have to solve it. That's where I'd want help.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Every planner says end-to-end. 'Anywhere in the world' and 'from start to finish' don't tell me what you actually do or who is accountable. It's not offensive, it's just the line I skim past.

journey.quote: For a parent chasing one side of the family, copy the names and reply columns into a separate file rather than handing over every address.
journey.reaction: Practical, and exactly what will happen with my mum. I also like that it says it's general information, not legal advice, rather than pretending otherwise.

journey.section: When a spreadsheet stops being enough
journey.quote: Once invitations are out and replies start arriving from guests in different countries, typing each one in by hand becomes the work.
journey.reaction: True, and it speaks to 'we don't want to spend our evenings on spreadsheets'. The Studio pitch is fairly soft, which I prefer.

journey.section: Planning the weekend around your guests
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins. Every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the best line on the page for me. AUD quotes and the fee in writing go straight at my worry about hidden costs and currency surprises.

unanswered_questions: Does the Wonderland Studio guest list carry the travel columns (flights, arrival, accommodation), or only RSVPs, plus-ones and dietary notes? Can I import this spreadsheet into it?
What does a Wedded Advisor actually do for guest travel, for example airport transfers for older guests, and who is accountable on the day itself?
Is there a real wedding with international guests I can look at to see how this played out?
Roughly what does Wedded Concierge cost, or how is the fee worked out?
Which is right for the event reply options: four or five?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic 'end-to-end' claim with nothing concrete behind it. Not hard-sell, but it's the same line every planner uses.

would_share_with: Partner (James), to agree the plus-one and children rule before we start
Mum, along with the privacy tip about a separate file for her side of the family

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The closing section's AUD and fee-in-writing points make me curious enough to look at the Concierge page, but this is a template post. I'd click through to see what's there, not to enquire yet. I'd want a real wedding and a clearer idea of what the Advisor actually handles first.

top_3_changes: Fix the reply options count so it matches the Events section. Old: "The four event columns offer the five reply options." New: "The four event columns offer the reply options listed under Events above."

Cut the generic end-to-end phrasing in the mid-article CTA so it reads less like every other planner. Old: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish." New: "A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, as your single point of contact."

Keep the closing section's AUD and fee-in-writing lines as they are. They are what moved me from 'free template' to 'maybe look at Concierge'. If the team has a published real wedding with international guests, the panel could consider linking it near the closing CTA (I can't supply the wording without inventing facts).

No invented brand facts; missing information listed under unanswered_questions
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, 'free', vendor names, fees, on-the-ground claims, room blocks, availability, or Advisor managing the guest list or visas

open_questions.question: The Events section lists four reply options (Not invited, Invited, Attending, Declined) but the Dropdowns section says 'the five reply options'. Which matches the actual .xlsx file? My suggested edit avoids stating a number, but the file should be checked.
Is there a published real wedding with international guests that could be linked near the closing CTA? For this persona that is the step between reading and enquiring.

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding guest list template', as no arrival context was given.
Persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated), so reactions reflect assumed rather than verified client behaviour.
